name: InterContinental Hotels Group PLC
moat_justification: A strong (not widest) franchisor moat: 20 brands, 145m+ member loyalty programme and global distribution create real owner switching costs and pricing power, proven by a 65.9% fee margin and an asset-light model needing almost no capital. It sits behind Marriott/Hilton on scale and loyalty depth, owners can reflag at contract end, demand is cyclical (FY2020 collapse), and rivals are pressuring owner fees — durable, but contestable.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override

one_liner: High-quality asset-light hotel franchisor, moat 7/10 - but at $164.25 the 3.0% owner-earnings yield leaves no path to the hurdle: weighted IRR 6.9%, weighted IV@15 $53.81, and even the super-bull case (9.9% IRR) clears neither 10% nor 15%; clears 15% only below ~$53.81.
moat_for: 20-brand portfolio (InterContinental, Holiday Inn family, Crowne Plaza, Kimpton, Six Senses) across 100+ countries — distribution owners pay to access
IHG One Rewards loyalty programme (145m+ members) driving direct bookings and repeat stays
Asset-light fee model: fee margin 65.9% in H1 2026 and only $28M capex in FY2025 (filing history) — high returns on capital and strong cash conversion
Development pipeline of 348k rooms, 33% of current system size (H1 2026 release), giving visible multi-year fee growth
Proven pricing power: fee margin +120bp in H1 2026 with ADR +2.5% alongside occupancy gains
moat_against: Third in scale behind Marriott and Hilton, with smaller loyalty ecosystems and less owner leverage in contested markets
Owners can reflag at contract end; conversion brands lower switching frictions across the industry
Cyclical RevPAR: FY2020 revenue fell to $2,394M from $4,627M in FY2019 (filing history) — travel demand tracks the consumer/business cycle and geopolitics
Owner fee pressure: rivals are cutting fees and granting concessions to hold owners (2026 earnings-season reporting)
Buyback-funded leverage: net debt 3.4x normalized owner's earnings (engine diagnostics)
